profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap way is named centro de datos trasbase Negratin, and very little of that description survives checking. Reverse geocoding the recorded position places the building at Los Alamillos, in the municipality of Huercal-Overa in Almeria province, not in Granada province as this registry previously recorded. The name also misspells the Spanish word trasvase, which means an inter-basin water transfer.

What the building stands on is clear from the surrounding map data. It sits directly over a mapped underground water pipeline named Conexion Negratin-Almanzora, recorded in OpenStreetMap with the operator Aguas del Almanzora. That is the Negratin to Almanzora transfer, which carries water out of the Negratin reservoir on the Guadiana Menor in Granada province across into the Almanzora valley in Almeria, one of the driest farming regions in Spain. Immediately around the building the map also records a small reservoir or regulating pond, farmland and greenhouse horticulture, and a 66 kilovolt overhead line running from Huercal-Overa to Velez-Rubio. A second building a few metres away, OpenStreetMap way 1075858826, carries the same data centre tag with no name on it at all.

The provenance of the tag matters here. Both buildings were created in a single edit on 4 July 2022 by a contributor with 19 changesets to their name, whose changeset comment reads mejoras sur de huercal overa, meaning improvements south of Huercal-Overa, and whose only recorded imagery source was Spanish PNOA aerial photography. Aerial photography can establish that a building exists and roughly what shape it is. It cannot establish what is inside it, who operates it, or whether it holds computing equipment serving anyone beyond the water transfer itself.

The honest reading is that this is a control, telemetry or pumping related structure belonging to the Negratin to Almanzora transfer, of the kind that houses supervisory control and data acquisition equipment monitoring flows, levels and valve positions along the conduit. Spanish water authorities routinely call such a building a centro de datos, and the phrase does not carry the meaning it has in the computing industry. It is not a commercial or enterprise data centre. No operator has published anything describing it as one, and this registry records no capacity, floor area, electrical service or ownership figure for it.

Rows like this one are the reason unreviewed aggregation of OpenStreetMap telecom tags inflates data centre counts, and the effect is strongest in rural areas, where a single mapper's reasonable guess about an unmarked shed beside a pipeline becomes a permanent database entry that later systems treat as a confirmed facility.
profile.research_note: Investigated 2026-09-05 as a suspected mistag and confirmed as one. Nominatim reverse geocode on the stored coordinates returns Los Alamillos, Huercal-Overa, Almeria, correcting this registry's prior Granada province placement. An OSM map bbox call around the point returns way/776731010, an underground water pipeline named Conexion Negratin-Almanzora with operator=Aguas del Almanzora, running directly beneath the building, plus a reservoir, greenhouse horticulture and a 66 kV line Huercal-Overa to Velez-Rubio. Sibling building way/1075858826 carries telecom=data_center with no name. Creating changeset 123205224 (2022-07-04, user 7FLYTROTTER7, 19 changesets total) is commented "mejoras sur de huerval overa" with imagery_used=PNOA Spain only, no survey or operator source. No data centre operator, capacity or power figure asserted. Written as an honest mistag page.
